_readme: Every raster image under public/ and src/assets/, and the text it carries.
A grep cannot read a PNG, so this file is the only place an image's claims are visible to a check.
Entries with "generator" are written by scripts/og/make_page_og.py and must not be edited by hand; their sha256 pins the file.
Entries with "transcribed" were typed by a human reading the image on that date. Re-transcribe when the image changes.
"depicts" names a constant in src/data/products.ts and the value drawn; tests/og-images.test.js fails when they differ.
"concerns" are known problems with an image's text, recorded rather than fixed.

text: WHICH CUSTOMER DATA SIGNALS ARE YOU CURRENTLY SENDING?
TICK THE PARAMETERS YOU ALREADY SEND TO SCORE YOUR SETUP
Low: most identifiers are not being sent
Share of the weighted checklist you send

Add email address: the highest-impact single signal. Hashed SHA256, sent server-side. Add phone number: second highest EMQ impact. Hashed E.164 format. Switch to server-side Events API: the browser pixel loses iOS conversions the server never would. Capture fbc from URL: enables precise click-level deduplication.

What this score is. It is this tool's own heuristic: a weighted checklist of the customer parameters you send, scaled by whether you send them from the browser, the server, or both. It is not a prediction of Meta's Event Match Quality and it does not read anything from your ad account. Meta's actual EMQ is reported per event in Events Manager → Data Sources → your pixel → Event Match Quality; this estimates the inputs that feed it, not the number Meta returns.

text: HOW OFTEN DO YOU MANUALLY UPDATE STOCK?
DO YOU USE STOCKY PURCHASE ORDERS?
WORKED EXAMPLE · A MID-SIZED STORE: CHANGE ANY ANSWER TO SCORE YOUR OWN

Stocky stopped working on 31 August 2026, and its APIs stopped that day with no grace period: anything that integrated with them is already broken and needs repointing at Shopify's own inventory data. Your archive is a separate matter: Shopify says read-only export access continues for at least 90 days after that date, with no end date published. Export it before you rebuild, and read the score above as how much reconstruction is left if you cannot. Plan your migration carefully. Export all Stocky data first. Map your SKUs to the new template before going live. Allow at least 4 weeks of parallel running to catch edge cases.

How this is scored. The risk score is this tool's own heuristic: six weighted inputs (monthly orders, active SKUs, manual stock edits, suppliers, purchase-order reliance and export habit), summed and capped at 100. The weights are a judgement about which of those hurts most when data disappears, not a measured model of migration outcomes, and no store's actual migration was used to fit them. Use it to rank your own situation, not to predict hours.
